mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household demand for equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (< -0.3) between GDPC1 YoY decline and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which depresses corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) during triggered periods in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the previous six-month average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative relationship (< -0.25) between INDPRO contraction and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 12-month averages for three consecutive months signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month avg AND RSAFS > 12-month avg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary tightening follows.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (< -0.3) between low unemployment duration and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
